title: Gabber dimension bound for torsion nearby cycles
statement: Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-algebra. Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $N\ge0$ is an integer and every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Let $V_f=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be the vanishing topos and $R\Psi_f=R\psi_{f,*}$ the nearby-cycle functor on constant-coefficient $\Lambda$-module sheaves, as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and every integer $q>2N$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_f(F[0]))$ on $V_f$ is zero. No Noetherian hypothesis, invertibility of $m$ on $S$, constructibility of $F$, or quasi-compactness of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Illusie, Around the Thom-Sebastiani theorem, Theorem 1.14, printed p. 15 (PDF page 15), read from the author PDF online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an oriented geometric point $z=(x,t,c)$ of $V_f$, with $s=f(x)$ and $c:S_{(t)}\to S_{(s)}$. Put $M=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)}$. The oriented-point cohomology theorem, applied with its second scheme equal to $S$ and $K=F[0]$, identifies $z^*R\Psi_f(F[0])$ with $R\Gamma(M,F|_M)$. Constant-coefficient inverse image is exact and commutes with forgetting scalars. The bounded-below evaluation/forget theorem therefore identifies the underlying abelian group of its degree-$q$ cohomology with $H^q(M,A)$, where $A$ is the underlying abelian sheaf of $F|_M$. Since $mF=0$, $mA=0$. It suffices to prove this group zero for $q>2N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the projective-local-model lemma to $f,x,N$. Write $B=S_{(s)}$ and obtain $p:P\to B$, $y$ and $\theta:X_{(x)}\simeq P_{(y)}$. Use $\theta$ to regard $M$ as $P_{(y)}\times_B S_{(t)}$ and $A$ as a torsion abelian sheaf on this scheme. Set $C=S_{(t)}$, $Z=P\times_B C$, let $p_C:Z\to C$ be the projection, and let $\tau:M\to Z$ be the map induced by $P_{(y)}\to P$. The model is proper with fibre dimension at most $N$, and is projective over the affine scheme $B$. All subsequent proper-base-change applications are to this model, not to $f$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: The strict localization $P_{(y)}$ is affine. The proper model $P$ is separated over affine $B$, so the separated-over-affine lemma makes $P$ separated as an absolute scheme. Thus the affine-source/separated-target lemma makes $P_{(y)}\to P$ affine; its base change $\tau$ is affine and therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are exactly the finiteness hypotheses needed for the strict-henselization stalk formula in the next step.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $Q=R\tau_*A\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$. Let $k$ be the separably closed residue field of $C$, put $Z_0=Z\times_C\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $i:Z_0\to Z$ be the closed geometric fibre and $u$ any geometric point of $Z_0$. The stalk formula gives $(\mathcal H^aQ)_u\simeq H^a(M\times_Z Z_{(u)},A)$. The specialization supplies a geometric point $t_B$ of $B$. Ind-etale invariance for $B=S_{(s)}\to S$ identifies $B_{(t_B)}$ with $C=S_{(t)}$, over $B$ with the chosen specialization. Thus $C\to B$ is a strict-localization structural map. Apply the base-change clause of ind-etale invariance to $Z=P\times_B C\to P$: it identifies $Z_{(u)}$ with $P_{(v)}$, for $v$ the image of $u$. In $M\times_Z Z_{(u)}$, the $C$-coordinate is forced to be that of $Z_{(u)}$, so the universal property of the fibre product identifies it with $P_{(y)}\times_P P_{(v)}$. The strict-local-intersection acyclicity lemma applies because $P$ is projective over affine $B$, and gives zero for $a>0$. Thus $i^{-1}Q$ is concentrated in degree zero. Write it as $H[0]$; $H=i^{-1}\tau_*A$ is annihilated by $m$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED. The acyclicity input is verified from Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme, Theorem 7.10 (etale case), pp. 14–15.

proof.text:
For every degree $q$, the Leray identification gives $H^q(M,A)=H^q(Z,Q)$. The complex $Q$ is bounded below and its cohomology is annihilated by $m$, since multiplication by $m$ on $A[0]$, hence on its derived image, is zero. Apply bounded-below proper base change to $p_C:Z\to C$ and the closed geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$. Properness is preserved under base change. The strict-local global-exchange lemma converts the closed stalk of this exchange into the restriction map $H^q(Z,Q)\to H^q(Z_0,i^{-1}Q)$: both the ring of $C$ and its residue field are strictly henselian and the residue homomorphism is local. Consequently
$$H^q(M,A)\cong H^q(Z_0,H).$$
No bounded-above hypothesis on $Q$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: The morphism $p_C$ is proper, and its fibre $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper with dimension at most $N$; the latter is a residue-field extension of a fibre of $p$, and the fibre-dimension base-change lemma preserves all its local dimensions, hence their supremum. Apply the proper torsion cohomological-dimension theorem to this fibre morphism and the torsion sheaf $H$: its $R^q$ direct image vanishes for $q>2N$. Over the strictly henselian field $k$, the closed-stalk/global-cohomology identification of the strict-local global-exchange lemma (the identity base-change square) identifies that stalk with $H^q(Z_0,H)$. Thus the group in step 5 is zero for $q>2N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $q>2N$ every oriented point $z$ therefore has $z^*\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_f(F[0]))=0$, since point inverse image is exact. Joint conservativity of oriented geometric points, applied to the morphism from this cohomology sheaf to the zero sheaf, proves $\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_f(F[0]))=0$. The argument was pointwise in $x,t,c$ and used only local finite type of $f$ and the given uniform fibre bound; it imposes no quasi-compactness, constructibility, or invertibility condition.

I checked those statements mathematically myself instead. I read Stacks 095U locally (lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper) and it matches lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound with no extra hypotheses. Steps: (1) the oriented-point cohomology node with Y=S, g=id gives RΓ(X_(x)×_{S_(s)}S_(t)), and the two lem-pe lemmas handle the change of scalars. (3) τ is affine, hence qcqs, because P is separated over affine B. (4) The stalk formula and ind-étale invariance, including its base-change clause, give Z_(u)≅P_(v) and M×_Z Z_(u)=P_(y)×_P P_(v); the acyclicity node then makes i^{-1}Q=H[0]. (5) Leray and bounded-below proper base change apply because Q is in D^+ with m-torsion cohomology and p_C is proper; the strict-local exchange with C→k gives H^q(M)=H^q(Z_0,H). (6) Z_0 is the geometric fibre over the image of C's closed point, which is generally not B's closed point, so node 1 needs the bound on every fibre, and it has it; 095U then gives vanishing for q>2N. (7) Joint conservativity finishes. New node 1 is true: base change to B, a quasi-finite map to A^d_B with d≤N, ZMT (Stacks 05K0), and a finite extension to P^d_B through the integral closure. The naive closure in P^n_B would not keep the bound, so the later split must use the finite extension. New node 2 is Artin's theorem on joins; P projective over affine B gives a common affine neighbourhood, and the empty and x=u cases hold. Neither new node restates the item or duplicates an existing node; I read the candidates found by rg. There is no cycle. I accept all 14 declared tool uses as generic black boxes (proper base change, stalk formula, strict-local exchange, Leray, 095U, fibre dimension, affine/separated permanence, stalk conservativity, the lem-pe coefficient lemmas), though their shared 'why' text is boilerplate.
